Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Nature & food

grow verb

get bigger

also grow bigger, grow taller, get bigger, you’ve grown

classical

Quint. 1.2.7: in lectīcīs crēscunt
Ov. Met. 2.643: crēsce, puer (Lewis & Short)

crēscō, crēscere, crēvī, crētum

verb, third conjugation, intransitive · Conjugation on Wiktionary

grow, get bigger

Of children, plants, animals and anything that grows of itself; crēvit, it has grown. With an adjective, English “grow” is “become”: senēscō, grow old (Traupman 77); jam advesperāscit, it’s growing dark (Ter. And. 581).

Other words

  • adolēscō, adolēscere, adolēvī, adultum — grow up, grow to full size

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Varro in Gell. 4.19.1: minusque adolēscere · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Of growing up to full size: children, young animals, crops.

Examples

  • Puer autem crēscēbat, et cōnfortābātur plēnus sapientiā

    And the child grew, and grew strong, filled with wisdomVulg. Lc. 2.40

  • puerōs inpūbēs compertum est, sī plūrimō cibō nimiōque somnō ūterentur, … corporaque eōrum inprōcēra fierī minusque adolēscere

    it has been found that if young boys eat too much and sleep too long, … their bodies stay short and grow lessVarro in Gell. 4.19.1

  • mīrātus dīcēs: ‘hoc, rogō, crēvit ubi?’

    you will say in wonder: ‘where, I ask you, did this grow?’Mart. 13.58.2

See also increase, develop, when you’re big, become, grow.
